newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Minister says Bangladesh banking system safe.
newsitem.headline: Minister says Bangladesh banking system safe.

text.p: Bangladesh Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria on Saturday said the country's banking system was not in crisis, and that fresh reforms were in the pipeline to strengthen the sector.
"Our banking system is absolutely safe. I urge all not to be misled by any false propaganda," he told a business conference in Dhaka.
"In fact, banks are now being run stronger than anytime in last 15 years. Monitoring (by the central bank) is much more effective than before," he said.

These were the first remarks by Kibria after newspapers last month quoted Bangladesh central bank governor Lutfar Rahman Sarkar as saying that the country's "banking system was on the verge of collapse" due to huge defaulted loans.
That triggered alarm among local and foreign bankers, and Sarkar later said he was misquoted in a press release issued by his office.
The finance minister has since remained quiet on the issue.
Central bank officials say the commercial banks in both private and public sectors were burdened with a total of 130 billion taka ($3 billion) in bad debt.
Kibria said on Saturday that out of the total the banks had recovered 1.5 billion taka by vigorous recovery efforts since his Awami League government took office in June last year.
Kibria said a new phase of financial sector reforms would start soon to streamline the banking sector.
The World Bank and Japan would finance the reforms, he said without elaborating.
